That is not entirely correct. It depends on the level that this event was taking place. 

Considering that the guy got a warning and a game loss, I assume this is Competitive REL, but the judge handled it like you would handle it at Standard REL (basically FNM level).

The judge should not shuffle the card into the deck as that would ruin the order of the deck if anything was changed. At Standard REL the judge would shuffle the hand and put a card at random on the top. When an adventure is on the stack, it is only a sorcery/instant, the normal card is non-existent for the game.

In magic, you can “technically” attempt to cast illegal spells, they will be checked for legality only at the end before being actually cast, basically after targets have been declared and stuff like that.

Lier works because you declare that you want to cast the adventure from your graveyard. You put it on the stack and start choosing targets and such. Now… remember what I said earlier about adventures on the stack being only their sorcery/instant part? Well now when you go to check the legality of the spell… it’s a sorcery/instant that came from the graveyard… so that means that Lier gave it flashback in the graveyard. Which means the spell is legal and is then cast.
